messages.content: Please find me any of the songs that I've played the most this week.

function.name: Music_3_PlayMedia
function.description: Initiates playback of a specified music track on a designated device. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

track.description: The title of the track to be played.

artist.description: The name of the artist performing the track.

device.description: The name or location of the device where the music will be played.

album.description: The name of the album that the track is from, if applicable.

function.name: Music_3_LookupMusic
function.description: Finds songs that align with the user's musical preferences based on the artist, album, genre, and release year. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

artist.description: The name of the artist performing the song. Use 'dontcare' to ignore this criterion.

album.description: The name of the album that the song is part of. Use 'dontcare' to ignore this criterion.

genre.description: The genre of the music. Use 'dontcare' to indicate no specific preference.

year.description: The year of the song's initial release. Format should be a four-digit number, e.g., '2001'. Use 'dontcare' to ignore this criterion.

message.content:
Sure! To help you find the songs you've played the most this week, could you let me know:

1. Which songs (or artists/albums) you think were played the most?
2. Any particular genre or year you'd like to focus on?

Once I have that information, I can search your library for matching tracks.
message.reasoning:
The user wants to find songs they've played the most this week. We need to use the Music_3_LookupMusic function. But we don't have data about what songs they've played. There's no context. We might ask clarifying question: which songs? Or maybe we can assume we have some data. But we can't guess. So we should ask clarifying question: do they want songs from their library? Or from last week's play history? We need more info.

We could ask: "Which songs have you played the most this week?" But that's basically asking them to provide the list. Alternatively, we could ask: "Do you want me to look up songs from your library that match your most played tracks this week?" But we need to know which songs those are. So we need clarification.

Thus respond asking for clarification.
